regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Your team may choose a combination when reducing tumour size is an important goal and you are fit for more intensive treatment. For advanced disease, treatment generally aims at control and symptom relief; a combination is not a guarantee of longer survival.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Locally advanced unresectable or metastatic soft tissue sarcoma
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Doxorubicin interacts with DNA and topoisomerase II, disrupting copying and repair. Its heart and tissue effects require particular care. Ifosfamide damages cancer-cell DNA. Its breakdown products can also affect the bladder, kidneys and brain. Mesna protects the bladder but does not prevent all kidney or brain effects.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: NCCP 00391: doxorubicin 20 mg/m² and ifosfamide 3000 mg/m² on each of days 1–3, repeated every 21 days for up to 6 cycles. Per-cycle totals are doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and ifosfamide 9000 mg/m². Mesna, hydration and other support continue for their prescribed periods.
key_points: This is NCCP 00391: doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and ifosfamide 9 g/m² per cycle. The two NCCP combination regimens have different doxorubicin doses and eligibility details. They must not be substituted for each other or for a published 10 g/m² ifosfamide regimen.

NCCP 00391: doxorubicin 20 mg/m² and ifosfamide 3000 mg/m² on each of days 1–3, repeated every 21 days for up to 6 cycles. Per-cycle totals are doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and ifosfamide 9000 mg/m². Mesna, hydration and other support continue for their prescribed periods.

Blood count and kidney/liver tests before each cycle. Neurological assessment before every ifosfamide dose; check for blood in urine before each dose and every 8 hours on treatment days. Monitor fluid balance, urine output and electrolytes according to the individual plan.

Mesna and prescribed hydration are essential bladder protection. NCCP requires G-CSF support and proton-pump inhibitor prophylaxis for this regimen; the team specifies product, dose and timing. Multi-day anti-sickness treatment needs a single reconciled prescription. Aprepitant may increase ifosfamide-related brain toxicity, so pharmacy must check the chosen plan.
regimen_profiles.review_status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.

treatment_rationale.summary: Doxorubicin interacts with DNA and topoisomerase II, disrupting copying and repair. Its heart and tissue effects require particular care. Ifosfamide damages cancer-cell DNA. Its breakdown products can also affect the bladder, kidneys and brain. Mesna protects the bladder but does not prevent all kidney or brain effects. A sarcoma multidisciplinary team reviews the exact pathology, disease extent, prior treatment, fitness and your priorities. Surgery and radiotherapy may help local control in selected circumstances; their role and timing are decided separately. Chemotherapy does not automatically replace an operation or radiotherapy. Supportive and palliative care can be used alongside cancer treatment to help symptoms and daily life.
treatment_rationale.setting: Locally advanced unresectable or metastatic soft tissue sarcoma
treatment_rationale.line: Locally advanced unresectable or metastatic soft tissue sarcoma
factors: Expert sarcoma pathology and subtype; resectability and disease extent; previous systemic treatment and anthracycline exposure; performance status, organ function, treatment goals and patient preference.
alternatives: Specialist sarcoma MDT review of histology- and setting-specific systemic options or trials, local surgery/radiotherapy when appropriate, and symptom-focused supportive care.
limitations: The trial used doxorubicin 75 mg/m² with ifosfamide 10 g/m² over four days. NCCP 00391 uses doxorubicin 60 mg/m² with ifosfamide 9 g/m² over three days. Trial response or survival figures are not validated estimates for this exact schedule. The advanced-disease trial does not establish neoadjuvant benefit.

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Your team may choose a combination when reducing tumour size is an important goal and you are fit for more intensive treatment. For advanced disease, treatment generally aims at control and symptom relief; a combination is not a guarantee of longer survival.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Locally advanced unresectable or metastatic soft tissue sarcoma
These cytotoxic regimens have no general tumour-biomarker selection rule; histological diagnosis and specialist review remain essential.
eligibility_orientation: Advanced unresectable or metastatic soft-tissue sarcoma.
ECOG 0–1; adequate hepatic, renal and bone-marrow function.
exclusion_orientation: Review current NCCP exclusions, pregnancy, hypersensitivity, organ function and source-specific baseline criteria.
important_cautions: Doxorubicin hepatic decisions use absolute bilirubin in µmol/L, not an assumed ULN of 20.
Bilirubin > 50 to < 51 µmol/L and CrCl exactly 10 mL/min are unallocated printed boundaries and require review.
CrCl exactly 50 mL/min is not assigned an ifosfamide dose by the printed table.
Current treatment-day counts and previous-cycle nadir with neutropenic fever are assessed separately.
Mucositis affects both cytotoxic components; grade ≥ 3 neurotoxicity stops ifosfamide only.
Source full-dose count thresholds differ between 00391 (> 1.5/> 100) and 00392 (≥ 1.5/≥ 100); do not copy one table to the other.

This is NCCP 00391: doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and ifosfamide 9 g/m² per cycle. The two NCCP combination regimens have different doxorubicin doses and eligibility details. They must not be substituted for each other or for a published 10 g/m² ifosfamide regimen.

The trial used doxorubicin 75 mg/m² with ifosfamide 10 g/m² over four days. NCCP 00391 uses doxorubicin 60 mg/m² with ifosfamide 9 g/m² over three days. Trial response or survival figures are not validated estimates for this exact schedule. The advanced-disease trial does not establish neoadjuvant benefit.

Identify the actual supplied ifosfamide product and reconcile its product information with the national regimen before treatment or restart. Current Irish Mitoxana 1 g (PA2299/028/001) lists contraindications at serum creatinine >120 micromol/L, bilirubin >17 micromol/L, or transaminases/alkaline phosphatase >2.5 times the local upper limit of normal. These named-product limits are stricter than portions of the national dose tables. They are not a universal replacement dose rule: known product contraindications require an ifosfamide hold and oncology/pharmacy reconciliation; an unknown product cannot be presumed safe.

Use actual serum creatinine and bilirubin with verified units and actual liver-enzyme results with their local upper limits. Creatinine clearance/eGFR is not serum creatinine, and absolute AST is not an assumed multiple of normal. Preserve the national regimen’s separate component-specific renal/hepatic decisions; do not invent a percentage, laboratory reference range or conversion to resolve the product conflict.

Current suspected ifosfamide encephalopathy or central-nervous-system symptoms require interruption of further ifosfamide administration and immediate assessment. This current-infusion decision is separate from whether future rechallenge is appropriate. Preserve the national grade 3-or-greater neurotoxicity stop for ifosfamide and the distinct doxorubicin rules; a normal current value does not erase a previous severe event.

premedication_and_prophylaxis: Confirm the full three-day treatment and post-treatment mesna/fluid plan, G-CSF injections, stomach protection and anti-sickness medicines before starting. Tell the team about sedating medicines or new confusion. Do not change fluid intake or medicines without the team’s advice.

Mesna and prescribed hydration are essential bladder protection. NCCP requires G-CSF support and proton-pump inhibitor prophylaxis for this regimen; the team specifies product, dose and timing. Multi-day anti-sickness treatment needs a single reconciled prescription. Aprepitant may increase ifosfamide-related brain toxicity, so pharmacy must check the chosen plan.
counselling: The team chooses suitable intravenous access and explains line care. Tell the nurse immediately about burning, pain, redness or swelling during an injection or drip. Do not wait for the visit to finish. If you have a port or PICC, agree dressing, flushing and removal arrangements. Confirm who manages the mesna pump and when it is disconnected; do not alter pump settings yourself.

Discuss fertility preservation before treatment. Avoid pregnancy and breastfeeding as directed. Your team must give written contraception and post-treatment precautions for every medicine, using current product information; the required duration may differ by medicine and between patients.
